title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-02-11
lineage: Akai GX636 direct tape head output  > Bottlehead tube tape pre w/a pair of Tesla tubes circa 1960  > Apogee Mini Me 24/96  > Apogee Mini DAC monitoring and mastering  > FLAC
source: SBD MR Technics RS 1506 @7.5 ips > Revox A77(Bob Menke)@7.5 ips > Revox A77(Pat Lee)@7.5 ips

ai_review.summary: High‑energy Spanish Jam and surprise Greg Allman vocals dominate this soundboard capture, though it cuts off abruptly before Shine On Me.
ai_review.review: The show bursts with a wild, busy Spanish Jam that even hints at Peter Green’s ominous slide work, and the unexpected Greg Allman vocal on The Love Light adds an extra thrill. Pigpen’s enthusiasm and Phil Lesh’s bass‑line reminiscent of a Caution Jam keep the momentum rolling, but the recording ends abruptly just before Shine On Me, leaving the performance slightly unfinished.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (4‑5) and enthusiastic comments highlight an outstanding performance; recording is a soundboard with good fidelity but the abrupt ending lowers the technical score slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear soundboard mix overall, but the track ends abruptly before Shine On Me, indicating a possible tape or file cut.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A jam‑heavy, densely layered second set that feels like a continuous improvisational flow; the energy stays high throughout despite the sudden cutoff at the end.

band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass line is highlighted as reminiscent of a Caution Jam, adding depth to the Spanish Jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Greg Allman's surprise vocal on The Love Light is noted; Peter Green's slide notes add flavor to the Spanish Jam.
